text:
maria: Quick question on proxy abort semantics — when the gateway receives a client cancel while upstream is still streaming, what should we do by default? Let upstream finish, cut connection immediately, or attempt transparent resume/fallback?

sam: Short answer: current behavior is immediate teardown. We've been leaning toward a soft-close window so we can resume if client reconnects quickly.

jon: We debated this in the last sync. Soft-close helps UX for flaky mobile clients but it complicates memory and billing (we keep kvcache pointers/state). Proposed soft window = 2s by default.

maria: Is that 2s per-request or per-connection? Major concern: if we keep streaming state for many concurrent requests we risk KV cache memory blowup.

li: Memory is the scary bit. Implementation idea: keep only metadata + pointers (no payload buffers), track per-route max_state_bytes and global soft_state_pool. Evict LRU when pool exhausted.

ana: Also: idempotency. For endpoints that are non-idempotent (side effects), we cannot transparently resume/redo without coordination. Need route-level flag.

sam: Proposal summary: 1) add lifecycle enum {live, soft_closing, closed} 2) soft_closing retains kvcache & route metadata for resume TTL (configurable) 3) resume only enabled for routes marked resume.enabled and mark side_effects=true to opt-out.

maria: Example route config I was thinking of:

```yaml
route:
  path: /chat/stream
  resume:
    enabled: true
    ttl_ms: 3000
    max_state_bytes: 1048576
  side_effects: false
```

jon: To add: eviction policy should prefer evicting oldest or largest state first; record metrics: resume_hits, resume_evictions, resume_bytes_used.

li: Implementation notes: store a small state record in an on-heap hashmap keyed by request-id (configurable key header). State record: route, kv_keys_snapshot, kernel_ptrs (opaque ids). Keep TTL index for expiry.

maria: Curious about billing: if we keep state for 3s, does that count as in-flight compute for customer? We need to align billing semantics with SLA.

sam: My take: don't charge token-inference while in soft_closing, but log it as reserved state; customers can opt into longer TTL for better UX (and will pay for reserved capacity in Dedicated).

deploy-bot: canary deployed edge-proxy:v2-soft-close-ttl (region=us-west-2) :rocket:

jon: Quick test notes: ran a reconnect churn test with wrk2 proxying to a local model and ~10k qps, resume hit ~82% with 3s TTL, memory delta ~ +120MB in kvcache metadata across 10k concurrent sessions.

li: Eviction thresholds: a) global soft_state_pool default 1GB b) per-route max_state_bytes default 1MB. If pool exceeded, evict oldest until under threshold and emit resume_eviction metric.

maria: Edge cases: 1) upstream closed while soft_closing — resume should fail fast and surface a clear 409/Resume-Failed header. 2) midstream auth refresh — if token expired during soft_close we must deny resume (auth is part of state key).

ana: Agree on 409 semantics. Also add audit log entry when resume used: request, original_ts, resumed_ts, route.

sam: I can sketch the RFC: state shape, lifecycle transitions, metrics, config knobs, and a migration plan (off by default, opt-in routes first).

maria: Great. Next steps: @sam please open the RFC PR. @li can you add memory budget knobs to Console and wire up resume_* metrics to the dashboard? I'll draft a short customer-facing note for Dedicated tenants.

li: Yep, will add dashboards. Want the metric names to be final before I wire them.

sam: I'll include metric names in the RFC: resume.hit, resume.miss, resume.eviction, resume.bytes_in_use, resume.ttl_expiry.

maria: Thanks all. I'll follow up once the RFC is up. :thumbsup:
